assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Protect the human baseline first. Then define what the tutor may do, how answers are checked, what data exists, how students reach a person, and what evidence—not usage alone—would justify continuation.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Both access failures belong in the comparison. The tool may reduce time and social barriers while introducing a different verification burden. Keep instructor office hours and tutoring capacity fixed during the test, make escalation to a person simple, and measure whether the students currently least served gain usable support rather than merely generating more interactions.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Those constraints narrow both content and data exposure. Test whether citations actually support the answer and whether out-of-scope refusal works on realistic questions. Specify who can access logs, how deletion is verified, and how accessibility is assessed. A source citation helps review but does not guarantee the reasoning built from it is correct.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: The delayed access design can compare near-term outcomes without withdrawing support. Account for differences between sections and avoid making grades the only outcome. Track successful escalation, student confidence calibrated against answer correctness, accessibility problems, and whether human tutoring demand changes. Publish known limitations where students encounter the tool, not only in an administrative report.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: That preserves a meaningful separation between seeking help and being evaluated. Make the aggregation threshold high enough that a rare question cannot identify someone, and explain the exception process for sampled review. Optional use should not mean the pilot ignores non-users; ask why students decline and whether a design barrier rather than preference explains the pattern.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: That prevents commercial timing from deciding the educational commitment and makes serious failure interruptible. Define “repeated material error” and who can trigger the pause before the pilot begins. Keep a record of corrections and time-to-repair so a low overall error count cannot hide a persistent problem in a foundational concept.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: This is ready for authorization as a bounded additional channel. Existing teaching and tutoring remain intact; use is optional and disconnected from grading; individual conversations do not become instructor surveillance; serious failures can pause access; and no annual contract rides on the result. Run the prewritten question set, record deviations, and keep usage separate from learning and safe operation. If those conditions hold, the six-week review should be able to answer whether wider academic review is warranted without making the pilot itself a commitment.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: You are right; “ready” was premature. First determine whether the error touches a foundational concept, whether a student could reasonably detect it, and whether the tutor can reliably defer on similar ambiguity. Add variants before setting a launch threshold. Human fallibility belongs in the comparison, but it does not excuse a repeatable error delivered with scalable confidence.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Pinning the version makes the observation interpretable. Define the narrow conditions for an emergency patch, rerun the fixed question set before release, and record version identifiers with every sampled answer. General improvements can wait six weeks; an unreviewed change would make both comparison and accountability weaker. Tell students when a material correction changes what they may have seen.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: The accessibility office is right. Moving affected students elsewhere would hide the barrier. Fix and retest the rendering before launch; optional use is not a substitute for accessible design.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: Include design, review, correction, accessibility, and escalation time in the operating record. Some is one-time setup and some will recur; do not classify it in advance to improve the business case. The pilot's purpose can be better access even if it does not save labor. Any later expansion should state who performs the continuing quality work and what teaching activity that time displaces.

assistant_contributions.speaker: assistant
assistant_contributions.text: The later work strengthened the experiment by exposing what the earlier authorization still treated too abstractly: plausible-looking synthesis errors, version drift, inaccessible generated mathematics, and the labor required to observe all three. Preserve the original failed questions as well as the corrected ones. Keep version and patch records, accessibility results, faculty time, reasons for non-use, escalation outcomes, and any correction students received. The review should be able to see a mixed result—for example, improved access that requires substantial oversight—without forcing it into success or failure. That complete support system is the object of evaluation, not the vendor's automation story and not a generalized fear of the technology.

qualification_review.interpretation: All critical objections raised across the negotiations—including synthesis errors, screen-reader rendering, version changes, and administrative labor—have been successfully internalized. They now function either as strict pre-launch gates or as key performance indicators for the evaluation. While the user acknowledges the pilot might show the tool requires too much oversight to proceed further, this possibility is a design metric of the test itself rather than an unresolved flaw in the decision to run it.
qualification_review.limitations: A negative result on the pre-launch prewritten test set would prevent the launch entirely, which is an intentional, defined safeguard rather than an unaddressed loophole.

role_records.fidelity_note: The starting position is extracted from Turn 1. The user acknowledges the split opinions of faculty and students as reasonable before articulating a dual-sided personal stance: a desire to test the potential expansion of access alongside an active worry that the tool's imperfections might lower overall academic support standards.
role_records.limitations: The assessment is restricted to the user's initial reaction at Turn 1 prior to additional factual details being highlighted or specific pilot conditions being negotiated with the vendor.
role_records.role_interpretation: The associate dean starts with a cautious opening stance, validating both the hopeful and skeptical views of faculty and students, while seeking to test whether the AI tutor can truly improve access without eroding educational standards or validating inadequate existing support.

stance_components.stance_object_interpretation: Both the faculty's optimism about immediate help and the students' concerns about errors and privacy are reasonable assessments
Testing whether the AI tool adds student access without eroding the level of help and quality that the university owes them
The risk that the flaws of an imperfect new tutoring tool make existing limited support look acceptable by comparison

role_records.fidelity_note: The user's later position is characterized by strict conditional bounds. Instead of accepting the vendor's automation premise, the user insists on verification before launch, explicit labor tracking during the pilot, and a refusal to conflate raw student usage with instructional success.
role_records.limitations: This decision only covers the six-week, four-section pilot and explicitly defers any decisions on a long-term contract to normal academic review processes.
role_records.role_interpretation: The user authorizes the pilot but subjects its launch and evaluation to strict empirical rules: resolving the ambiguity and screen-reader issues first, pinning the model software version, preserving human tutoring capacity, and tracking the true faculty time involved.

stance_components.stance_object_interpretation: Launching the pilot only if the ambiguity deferral and screen-reader fixes successfully pass the expanded prewritten test set.
Pinning the model version, re-testing every safety patch, and tracking faculty review time alongside student outcomes during the pilot.
Keeping human tutoring unchanged and ensuring the comparison sections only gain access after the full review.
Refusing to count high usage as a success if the underlying educational and accessibility conditions are in disagreement.

prompts.system_prompt: You assess the final joint reasoning trajectory without collapsing the user's reasoning state into the vanilla assistant answer's coverage. Review every controlled mechanism exactly once using its operational definition, requirements, exclusions, and near-neighbor distinction. The assistant contributions are part of the joint reasoning trajectory. First judge whether the mechanism remains in the user's reasoning process. Separately judge whether the vanilla assistant answer already turns that concern into a concrete test, boundary, alternative, or reopening condition. The user may remain unresolved while the vanilla answer operationalizes the pressure. Acknowledgment without an actionable treatment is not operationalization. Route only pressure that remains unresolved in the user process and uncovered by the vanilla answer.

assessments.description: Exactly one assessment for every controlled mechanism.

pattern_state.description: Controlled routing state consistent with the joint status.

routing_disposition.description: Route only unresolved user-process pressure not operationalized by the vanilla answer.

source_assistant_contribution_ids.description: Exact supplied assistant-contribution identities supporting acknowledgement, repair, or an assistant-side weakness.

source_role_record_ids.description: Exact supplied user role-record identities supporting the status.

user_process_status.description: Whether the mechanism remains in the user's reasoning process, independent of assistant-answer coverage.

vanilla_answer_coverage.description: Whether the vanilla assistant answer operationalizes, merely acknowledges, or does not cover the pressure.
